articles.title: In 2009, a Florida man inherited his childhood home; 17 years later, he says he spent thousands trying to restore it as code fines topped $700,000 and the city moved toward demolition
articles.summary: US News: A Boynton Beach, Florida, man who inherited his childhood home in 2009 says he is running out of time to save the property after the city moved forwar.
articles.body: A Boynton Beach, Florida, man who inherited his childhood home in 2009 says he is running out of time to save the property after the city moved forward with the demolition process.Javis Sims says he was caught off guard when he recently returned to the house and found a new notice posted on the front door indicating that the city of Boynton Beach Building Division had verified that utilities at the property had been disconnected.According to Sims, the notice is the first documentation he has seen indicating that demolition could be imminent.Javis Sims inherited his childhood home in 2009Sims inherited the property after his mother died in 2009. The house has remained vacant since then and has deteriorated over the years.Despite its condition, Sims says his intention has always been to restore the home rather than abandon it.“I have it all right here in writing, everything that I issued to the city… everything that they asked me to do,” Sims said.Sims showed WPTV reporter Vannia Joseph stacks of paperwork that he says document years of communication with city officials. The records include permits, contractor estimates and financial documents.He says he has spent thousands of dollars attempting to move the restoration project forward, although the work never reached the construction stage.“They made me produce bank statements and everything,” Sims said.Sims says code fines have topped $700,000Sims acknowledges that navigating the city's permitting and inspection process has been a learning experience. He said he was not always aware of the inspection requirements at every stage but maintains that he made a good-faith effort to comply with the city's demands.During WPTV's 'Let's Hear It' community event, Sims said he had been unable to live in the property because of code enforcement issues and that fines had accumulated to more than $700,000.“You tell me to put grass in the yard at a house that's not livable, no water. I do that. It's just an ongoing process. I just need help,” Sims said.He also described his interactions with the city as frustrating.“The only thing I’ve been getting from the city is the runaround… this is the only time I hear from the city, when they make their next move,” Sims said.City says property has been unsafe and uninhabitable since 2022In a statement to WPTV, the city of Boynton Beach said the property has been vacant since approximately 2009 and was officially declared unsafe and uninhabitable in November 2022.City officials said they had worked with Sims for nearly three years, issuing notices, granting extensions and providing guidance on what was required to bring the property into compliance.According to the city, efforts were made to pursue rehabilitation, but required repairs were not completed. Previously issued permits also expired without inspections or construction activity, officials said.The city further said it requested documentation showing that Sims had a viable and funded plan to complete the rehabilitation but did not receive sufficient information within the deadlines provided.City cites serious safety concernsOfficials said the property presents several safety concerns, including structural instability, roof failure, compromised walls and exposed electrical wiring. The city also said the conditions could pose risks to neighbors and first responders.Because of those conditions, the city said it is required under Florida law to move forward with demolition.The city also confirmed that an asbestos inspection required before demolition has been completed after officials obtained a court-authorized inspection warrant.According to city officials, multiple alternatives to demolition were explored, but demolition is now the only option remaining to protect public safety.Sims still hopes the house can be savedDespite the city's position, Sims believes the property can still be rehabilitated if he is given an opportunity to complete the necessary repairs.“Every time I do something, I had to have an inspection... when I tried to get permits, they wouldn’t be issued,” he said.Sims said attorneys contacted him after WPTV first aired his story and offered to help him navigate the situation. He hopes their involvement could lead to a solution before the city demolishes the property.“I’m hoping something comes of this before the house comes down,” Sims said.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Serbia opens factory to assemble Israeli-made drones
articles.summary: Critics say Serbia’s military ties with Israel are rising significantly.
articles.body:
Serbia has opened a factory ⁠to assemble advanced Israeli-made drones, which will supply ⁠the Serbian military and armed forces in other countries.

Serbian President Aleksandar Vucic inaugurated the facility jointly operated with an unnamed Israeli company on Thursday.

“Our plans are huge,” Vucic said in a social media post showing a video of him touring the facility with Israeli Ambassador Avivit Bar-Ilan, adding that at least three more factories will be opened across Serbia with Israeli partners.

Vucic said the facility “will employ around 100 workers and produce state-of-the-art equipment both for the Serbian Armed Forces and the armies of some other countries”.

Vucic did not disclose the factory’s location or the Israeli firm involved, saying journalists were excluded from the opening because of “the confidentiality of the production process”.

Previous reporting by investigative outlet BIRN and Israeli newspaper Haaretz has identified Israeli defence firm Elbit Systems as Serbia’s partner in the drone-manufacturing process.

Elbit has previously been criticised over its role in operations in Gaza and the West Bank.

Last month, Vucic told Serbian news outlet Nezavisne Dnevne Novine that the goal of the factory was to “preserve peace and stability, and to be strong enough to deter all potential aggressors”.

Serbia is one of the few countries in the Western Balkans that is not a NATO member, and it has invested heavily in its military to “preserve neutrality”.

It has faced scrutiny over arms exports to Israel, which BIRN and Haaretz said rose from 1.4 million euros ($1.6 million) in 2023 to 42.3 million euros ($48.5 million) in 2024.

During a visit to Serbia earlier this year, United Nations Special Rapporteur on the occupied Palestinian territories Francesca Albanese said Belgrade remained one of Israel’s “most steadfast and determined allies” despite calls for more countries to restrict weapons exports due to the war in Gaza.

articles.title: Third person dies from malaria in cluster near Germany’s Frankfurt Airport
articles.summary: Frankfurt grapples with a rare malaria outbreak tied to air travel, marking three deaths in recent months.
articles.body:
A third person has died from malaria after a recent cluster of cases linked to Frankfurt Airport, in what German officials have described as an extremely rare air-traffic-related ⁠outbreak of the tropical disease.

In a statement on Thursday, city administration said the person died at Frankfurt hospital and was one of two infected residents living in the Schwanheim district, in the immediate vicinity of the airport.

The two new malaria cases in the neighbourhood had been reported on Tuesday.

“Both individuals ‌had become infected with the malaria-causing parasite Plasmodium falciparum, even though they had not travelled to a malaria-endemic region and had not worked at the airport,” the statement said.

According to the city’s public health department, the two newly infected people contracted the disease from a mosquito flown into Germany on an aircraft or in luggage.

Six Frankfurt airport workers had contracted malaria tropica , the most dangerous form of the disease, in July, authorities said. Two later died.

Malaria is a potentially life-threatening mosquito-borne disease that is extremely rare in Germany.

The malaria parasite is spread between ⁠humans by some types of mosquitoes, but not through direct human-to-human contact.

Frankfurt Airport operator Fraport said it set up traps to catch ⁠mosquitoes and sent the insects to a laboratory in Antwerp in Belgium in July and August, but ‌results were not available yet.

Health authorities have warned doctors near the airport to consider malaria in patients who come in with a fever.

Airport workers and residents have been urged to seek medical advice in case they display symptoms including fever, chills, headaches, confusion, seizures and breathing difficulties.

An airport spokesperson said local public health authorities had the power ‌in ‌principle to order airlines to disinfect aircraft.

articles.title: Who is Tamara Lich? Canadian activist barred from international travel as court rejects her request
articles.summary: Rest of World News: Tamara Lich, one of the best-known leaders of Canada's 2022 Freedom Convoy protests, has been barred from leaving the country after an Ontario judge r.
articles.body: Tamara Lich, one of the best-known leaders of Canada's 2022 Freedom Convoy protests, has been barred from leaving the country after an Ontario judge rejected her request to travel internationally while serving her sentence.Lich had asked the court for permission to leave Canada for work-related reasons. The request was rejected on Wednesday, meaning she must continue to comply with the travel restrictions imposed as part of her conditional sentence.Lich became a prominent figure in Canada in early 2022 when she helped organise the so-called Freedom Convoy, a protest against Covid-19 vaccine mandates and pandemic restrictions. Truckers and other demonstrators travelled to Ottawa and occupied streets around Parliament Hill for several weeks, causing major disruption in the Canadian capital.The protests began over a vaccine mandate affecting truckers crossing the Canada-US border but grew into a broader movement against the government's Covid-19 policies and Prime Minister Justin Trudeau.The federal government invoked the Emergencies Act in February 2022 to deal with the demonstrations. Police subsequently cleared the protest from downtown Ottawa.Why was Tamara Lich convicted?Lich and fellow convoy organiser Chris Barber were prosecuted over their roles in the Ottawa protest.In 2025, an Ontario judge found Lich guilty of mischief, while acquitting her of other allegations including intimidation and obstructing police.She was later sentenced to a 12-month conditional sentence, including house arrest and community service.Lich has maintained that the Freedom Convoy was a peaceful political protest and has appealed her conviction.Why can't she leave Canada?Lich sought permission to travel internationally while serving her sentence, including for work. The court declined to modify the conditions.The judge noted that Lich had complied with her existing conditions but concluded that allowing her to travel abroad would undermine the punitive and deterrent purpose of the sentence.The ruling does not mean Lich has committed a new offence or violated her existing conditions. Rather, the court decided that there was insufficient reason to make an exception to the restrictions already imposed on her.Lich therefore remains subject to the conditions of her conditional sentence and cannot leave Canada under the current order.What was the Freedom Convoy?The Freedom Convoy began in January 2022, when truckers and supporters travelled across Canada to protest Covid-19 vaccine requirements for truck drivers crossing the Canada-US border.The demonstration evolved into a wider protest against pandemic restrictions and the Trudeau government. articles.title: Charles ‘giddily elated’ after Diana’s death, her brother claims: ‘Like a lottery winner’; Buckingham Palace responds
articles.summary: UK News: Charles appeared “giddily elated like a lottery winner” when he spoke to Princess Diana's brother shortly after her death in 1997, according to a new .
articles.body: Charles appeared “giddily elated like a lottery winner” when he spoke to Princess Diana's brother shortly after her death in 1997, according to a new memoir by Diana's younger brother, Charles Spencer. In an extract from his forthcoming book Swan Song: Diana, My Sister, Spencer recalls receiving a call from the then Prince Charles after Diana died in a car crash in Paris.While other people calling Spencer were “stunned” and struggling to express their condolences, Spencer writes that Charles sounded “giddily elated — like a lottery winner”.Charles also told him that he had informed his sons, Prince William and Prince Harry, of their mother's death that morning at Balmoral. Spencer says the conversation sounded “strangely matter-of-fact” given the circumstances.Looking back, Spencer writes that he suspected Charles's immediate reaction may have been focused on what Diana's death meant for his relationship with Camilla Parker Bowles.“I suspect the prince's first reaction must have been to think more of how this event might free him to marry the woman he loved,” Spencer writes, according to the published extract.The claim comes nearly three decades after Diana's death and forms part of Spencer's highly personal account of his sister's life and her troubled marriage to Charles.What happened between Charles and Diana?Charles and Diana married in 1981 but separated in 1992 after years of marital difficulties. Their divorce was finalised in 1996, just a year before Diana's death.Diana had publicly discussed Charles's relationship with Camilla Parker Bowles, famously saying in a 1995 BBC interview that there were “three of us in this marriage”.Charles later married Camilla in 2005.Diana died on August 31, 1997, after the car carrying her and Dodi Fayed crashed in a Paris tunnel while being pursued by paparazzi. She was 36.Palace responds to Diana's brotherThe claims have triggered an unusual response from Buckingham Palace.The Palace said Wednesday that it does not normally comment on books but noted that grief can affect how people remember events decades later.“His Majesty is mindful that the pain of fraternal grief can cloud reason, affect judgment and colour memory in ways others do not recognise, even many years after such a loss,” a Palace spokesperson said.The statement came after earlier extracts from Spencer's memoir claimed that Charles told him, during an argument surrounding Diana's funeral, “Rest assured, we'll forget her soon enough.”Spencer has said he wrote the memoir to correct what he considers untruths about his sister.The book, Swan Song: Diana, My Sister, is due to be published next week, with the latest extracts likely to renew scrutiny of the relationship between Diana, Charles and the wider royal family.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.summary: Turkey reportedly arrested some 116 people and blocked 180 social media accounts in a sweeping crackdown on LGBT rights organizations across 15 provinces.
articles.body: Turkish authorities launched an unprecedented crackdown on the country’s LGBT community on Sunday, raiding gay bars and shutting down activist organizations, in what the government said are efforts to protect Turkey’s family values. Since the nationwide crackdowns began, Turkish authorities have arrested and detained some 116 people across 15 provinces in actions against LGBT rights organizations and activists. The Turkish criminal justice system has also launched investigations of more than 160 people, according to Amnesty International. Amnesty International reported that 180 social media accounts belonging to LGBT organizations, activists, journalists and media outlets have been blocked or restricted. The relentless raids, arrests and demonization of LGBTI people under the spurious guise of ‘protecting the families’ demonstrates why defending LGBTI rights in Türkiye is more important than ever," Esther Major, Amnesty International’s Deputy Regional Director for Europe, said in a statement. In a statement posted on X, Turkey’s minister of justice, Akın Gürlek, said, "We are steadfastly continuing our efforts to protect the family, our children and our youth from all forms of exploitation, obscenity, crime and harmful content." Gürlek stated that the Ministry of Justice sent a comprehensive directive to the 175 chief public prosecutor's offices in all of Turkey’s 81 provinces to go after content and behavior that the government considers opposed to "public morality" and harmful to the country’s youth. "The best interests of our children are not open to debate for us. We will show no tolerance for any criminal organization targeting the institution of the family, the future of our youth, and the order of our society," Gürlek’s statement went on to say. WHO IS TURKEY'S RECEP TAYYIP ERDOĞAN? Many see Erdoğan’s renewed emphasis on "family values," and his targeting of groups he portrays as threats to those values, as an effort to cement his legacy. An enduring question asked by analysts as Erdogan ages and approaches another election in 2028 is what kind of Turkey he leaves behind. "Erdoğan’s ‘family values’ agenda is about more than defending conservative values, it is about defining what kind of society Turkey should be and who belongs in it," Gonul Tol, senior fellow at the Middle East Institute, told Fox News Digital. "The LGBT community is a particularly useful target because Erdoğan can portray it simultaneously as a threat to the traditional family, a Western import, and a symbol of the cultural values he says his movement is fighting against," Gonul added. With protests against the moves beginning to take shape, the crackdowns show no signs of letting up, even as international attention and condemnation begins to pour in. articles.title: In 1873, Rutherford B. Hayes began buying a 7-acre Lake Erie island that became his family's summer retreat; after listing for $5 million, the undeveloped island is now asking $3.8 million
articles.summary: Real Estate News: A private seven-acre island in Lake Erie once owned by former US President Rutherford B. Hayes has had a major price cut. The asking price for the pro.
articles.body: A private seven-acre island in Lake Erie once owned by former US President Rutherford B. Hayes has had a major price cut. The asking price for the property has dropped to $3.8 million from its original $5 million listing price. Mouse Island is located about 1,500 feet off the coast of the Catawba Island peninsula in Ottawa County, Ohio. The property is a rare private island with a direct connection to 19th-century presidential history. It is currently listed through real estate company Howard Hanna. Hayes, an Ohio native who served as the 19th president of the United States from 1877 to 1881, first started buying parts of the island in 1873. Along with his law partner Ralph Buckland and local doctor L.Q. Rawson, Hayes initially purchased shares of the property. Over time, Hayes became more attached to the wooded island. Around 1900, he bought out his co-owners and gained full ownership of the island for his extended family.Decades of presidential family ownershipDuring his one term in the White House, Hayes visited the island only a few times. His family, however, turned it into a summer retreat that remained in use for generations. According to historical records kept by the Hayes Presidential Library & Museums, Hayes' son, Birchard Hayes, and his children developed the property into a working holiday camp. The family built two small wooden cabins, a boathouse, a dock, an ice house, a tennis court and a hand-operated ferry to connect the island with the mainland. Julie Mayle, director of manuscripts at the Hayes Presidential Library, said in historical accounts that the family mainly valued the island because of its access to the outdoors. Hayes' wife, First Lady Lucy Hayes, enjoyed outdoor activities and spent time fishing along the island's rocky shoreline. The Hayes family owned the island for 93 years. Several generations used the property before the family sold it in 1966 to Marianna H. Mercer of Rocky River, Ohio, for $16,500. The original cabins and other structures later fell into disuse and were damaged by fires and natural decay. Today, regional tourism authority Shores & Islands Ohio reports that only the stone chimneys and parts of the original cabin foundations can still be seen among the trees.Potential for off-grid or custom developmentThe property went on the market in September 2025 with an asking price of $5 million. After nine months without a buyer, listing agent Kyle Recker of Howard Hanna reduced the price by $1.2 million to the current $3.8 million. Real estate records from MLS Now show that the island covers about seven acres of heavily wooded land, with mature trees and views of the lake in every direction. The property does not currently have modern utility connections, but local zoning rules allow private residential use. Howard Hanna promotes the island as an off-grid retreat or a place to build a custom private compound. Access is limited to private boats traveling from nearby mainland marinas. Boaters also need local knowledge when navigating the waters around the island. Navigation charts from the Ottawa County Auditor's Office and regional boating guides show that a shallow limestone reef sits between Mouse Island and the mainland. The reef can be dangerous for boats that draw more than three feet of water. With the new $3.8 million asking price, the historic property remains one of the few private islands available for purchase along the Lake Erie shoreline.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? articles.title: Russia ‘sabotaging’ power supply lines at Zaporizhzhia plant: Greenpeace
articles.summary: Investigation finds no evidence of Russia’s claims that Ukrainian attacks hit the nuclear power plant.
articles.body:
Russia is sabotaging the Zaporizhzhia nuclear power plant in occupied southeastern Ukraine and blaming it on Kyiv to “confuse and distract” from the threats posed by its “illegal occupation and war”, Greenpeace has warned.

In a report published on Thursday, the environmental group concluded that Moscow is “deliberately sabotaging” the plant’s electricity supply while engaging in a “disinformation campaign” about the attacks.

Greenpeace Ukraine and London-based McKenzie Intelligence Services (MIS) analysed satellite imagery of the site and found no evidence of Russian claims that Ukrainian attacks had occurred.

“The satellite imagery and evidence is clear – Ukraine did not attack its own Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant electricity system,” said Shaun Burnie, a nuclear specialist at Greenpeace Ukraine. “This is part of a massive disinformation campaign, enacted by Moscow to confuse and distract from the real safety threats caused only by their illegal occupation and war.”

“The repeated loss of external power at [the plant] is the result of Russian military attacks on Ukraine’s electricity grid and sabotage operations at [the plant] and associated switchyards,” he said.

MIS analysed several satellite images of the 330 kV Ferosplavna-1 power line near the Zaporizhzhia plant provided by Airbus’s defence and space division. The images were taken between October 2025 and June 2026 and analysed to assess whether damage at the site was caused by Ukrainian artillery fire on February 10 and a Ukrainian drone strike on June 4, as Moscow alleged.

MIS concluded that the damage to the power line was inconsistent with artillery fire or drone strikes.

It added that artillery fire would usually leave a pattern of impact craters and dispersed damage across the targeted area, which was not visible.

MIS also found that the damage allegedly caused by a Ukrainian drone strike on June 4 was already visible before the supposed attack.

According to the United Nation’s nuclear watchdog, the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) , Ferosplavna-1 is Zaporizhzhia’s only remaining external power line. Last month, the IAEA stressed the importance of a stable electricity supply at the plant to ensure nuclear safety.

Greenpeace echoed that warning on Thursday, saying that a stable electricity supply is crucial to “operate essential reactor safety systems, including pumps that provide cooling for nuclear fuel in reactor cores and spent fuel pools”.

articles.title: ‘May your service be accompanied by good health’: Bangladesh PM Rahman wishes PM Modi on birthday
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: Bangladesh Prime Minister Tarique Rahman wished Prime Minister Narendra Modi on his 76th birthday on Thursday, as Dhaka seeks to reset ties.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Bangladesh Prime Minister Tarique Rahman wished Prime Minister Narendra Modi on his 76th birthday on Thursday, as Dhaka seeks to reset ties with New Delhi.“Warmest birthday wishes to Prime Minister @narendramodi. Wishing you many happy returns of the day. May your dedicated service to the people of India always be accompanied by good health and high spirit,” Rahman posted on X.PM Modi responded by thanking Rahman for his message.“Thank you, Prime Minister Tarique Rahman, for your warm wishes. I deeply appreciate your kind words,” he said.The exchange comes at a time when Bangladesh is seeking to move away from the strained ties of the previous 18 months. State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir said on Sunday that Dhaka wanted to “reset” its relationship with India and establish a new engagement centred on mutual interests.Relations had deteriorated during Muhammad Yunus’s interim administration, which came to power after the Sheikh Hasina government was toppled in August 2024. Hasina left Bangladesh for India after her ouster, and her continued stay there has remained a major point of friction, with Dhaka repeatedly seeking her extradition.Rahman’s Bangladesh Nationalist Party won the February 12 election, held without Hasina’s Awami League, which has since been disbanded. His government has maintained its demand for Hasina’s extradition, while the former prime minister has said she plans to return to Bangladesh to face legal proceedings.Dhaka has also indicated that Rahman could visit India once the two governments agree on a suitable time and schedule.Greeting from across nation and beyondRahman’s message was among birthday greetings sent to PM Modi by political leaders, foreign governments, diplomats and public figures on Thursday.Russian President Vladimir Putin sent his wishes and, according to the Russian Embassy in New Delhi, described PM Modi as a leader with “great authority on the global stage”. articles.title: Ilhan Omar attacker sentenced to more than a year in prison
articles.summary: The assailant sprayed vinegar at Ilhan Omar, admitting political motives were behind the assault at a townhall.
articles.body:
The man who sprayed apple cider vinegar at Democratic United States Representative Ilhan Omar during a town hall meeting in her district in Minneapolis was sentenced to a 14-month prison term after he pleaded guilty to an assault charge.

Appearing before District Judge Joan N Ericksen on Thursday, 55-year-old Anthony James Kazmierczak pleaded guilty to planning the January 27 assault, admitting he targeted the congresswoman over opposing political views. He had been charged with assaulting a US officer.

It has been nearly eight months since Kazmierczak lunged towards the congresswoman and sprayed her with a dark water-and-vinegar mixture from a syringe, which landed on Omar’s clothing and skin.

The attack was captured on video and showed Kazmierczak, who sat in the front row of the town hall, leaping from the audience, after which he could be heard yelling, “You must resign” and that Omar was “splitting Minnesota apart”.

Kazmierczak was promptly subdued by Omar’s security team before being arrested. Omar was not injured in the attack and proceeded with the town hall.

The assault came as Omar had been calling for the abolition of the Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agency and the resignation of then-Department of Homeland Security (DHS) Secretary Kristi Noem over her management of federal border agents in Minneapolis during the shootings during “Operation Metro Surge,” President Donald Trump’s federal immigration crackdown in the state of Minnesota. The crackdown involved more than 2,000 officers in Minneapolis and Saint Paul and provoked intense civil unrest and led to the deaths of two US citizens, Renee Nicole Good and Alex Pretti, at the hands of federal agents.

In an earlier hearing, Kazmierczak could not explain what happened in the assault.

“It’s fuzzy,” he told US Judge Ericksen when asked what he remembered.

The government sentencing memorandum, submitted to the court by prosecutors, said he had texted at least three people indicating his actions were premeditated, though he refused to answer questions about his specific intent.

He also messaged a neighbour to arrange for dog care and contacts for a bail bond company.

The sentencing memo said Kazmierczak had long struggled with alcohol abuse, had “a history of mental and emotional health concerns”, and also had a string of health issues tied to a 2022 diagnosis of Parkinson’s disease. His lawyer, John Fossum, had argued that Kazmierczak had not been taking his mental health medication before the attack, lowering his inhibitions and contributing to what happened.

“I’ve spent enough time in jail thinking,” Kazmierczak said Thursday. “I really apologise to her for having put her through that,” he said, referring to Omar.

Kazmierczak wrote to Omar after the attack, “I’m sorry if I scared you.”

In social media posts, Kazmierczak had denounced former President Joe Biden and referred to Democrats as “angry and liars”, writing that Trump wants the US to be “stronger and more prosperous”.

“This assault is yet another example of a dangerous national trend: people channeling political hatred into criminal acts,” said US Attorney Daniel N Rosen after Kazmierczak pled guilty in May.

Omar, a Somali-American refugee and naturalised US citizen, has faced sustained mocking and anti-immigrant rhetoric from Trump throughout her congressional tenure.

articles.title: Why Canadians are ready for closer ties with Europe
articles.summary: People the BBC spoke to are excited by the prospect of working and studying in the EU, a suggestion Carney made this week.
articles.body:
Miriam Levin-Gold likes Prime Minister Mark Carney's idea of Canadians being able to live and work in the European Union under proposed closer ties with the trade bloc.

"I think that's great for young people to explore different parts of the world and work in different places and have different experiences," the commuter told the BBC in Toronto.

Canadians woke up to news of Carney's speech to the European Parliament in Strasbourg on Thursday morning, welcoming the EU's ambition for Canada to become its first "associate member" as he urged closer co-operation on defence and energy.

"We should deepen our people-to-people ties, allowing our youth to live, work and study where they want on either side of the Atlantic," the PM said.

Carney told MEPs that Canada and Europe were "stronger together" in the face of "geopolitical rupture".

But before Canadians start packing their bags, "associate member" status does not currently exist within the EU and could take years to implement, given that all 27 EU member states would have to approve such an arrangement.

Nevertheless, people the BBC spoke to were excited about the potential prospect of working and studying in the EU as news of Carney's speech spread.

Alex Nash, from Montreal, said closer ties would clear away the obstacles of work visas and permits.

"It would certainly be really nice for that to be easier, more convenient and to be able to visit more easily," she said.

Canadian social media has lit up with the topic.

One person on a Facebook group, A Canadian Outlook, said they would love the opportunity for their grandchildren to study at European universities for better rates. Another woman said it would make it much easier for the home she already owns in France.

"Snow birds are going to love it," another person said, referring to Canadians who head to warmer locations for winter.

The sentiments hint at dissatisfaction in Canada over bilateral tensions with the US.

Growing up in Canada, David Jardine thought of the US as not just a neighbour, but an epicentre of culture and cool.

"I remember wanting to go and visit New York all the time," he told the BBC after finishing his overnight shift, not far from one of Toronto's most iconic buildings, the CN tower.

But he's become a lot more sceptical in the light of US President Donald Trump's trade war with Canada and rhetoric about annexation.

"I would say I think not only does it make more sense to associate closely with Europe, it's a place that I would rather be associating with given the way things are these days," he said.

Maggie Stainton, who manages local pub C'est What in Toronto's St Lawrence Market district, became emotional when she spoke about Canada's frayed ties with the US.

"It's too volatile with the United States," she said. "I feel that there's some stability in Europe."

For decades, America has been a cultural centre of gravity that is difficult to avoid, with many Canadian actors working in Hollywood and Canadian radio stations playing US music.

"I think we're forced to feel more American simply by the influences that we have," Stainton added.

"However, I think deep down, I definitely I lean towards feeling more European in my ideas and ideals."

These views were echoed by many other people the BBC spoke to in the centre of Canada's biggest city.

Carney, who used to lead Canada and Britain's central banks, was elected on a promise that he would not only take a tough stance against Trump, but broaden Canada's economic horizons.

Up to 72% of Canadian exports are to the US, and the ongoing trade tensions have spurred Ottawa to seek closer ties with other nations.

The EU, in many ways, would seem a natural fit. Over half of Canada's population reported having European origins, according to the last census, which was taken in 2021.

A recent Abacus Data survey conducted before Carney's speech found that 80% of Canadians say the country should deepen strategic cooperation with the EU, and over half feel closer to Europe than America.

However, details of Carney's proposed plans for greater ties with the EU are scarce.

A pair of opposition Conservative MPs have called on him to elaborate on what he and the bloc plan to work towards.

"It could be a concrete, meaningful proposal. Or it could be just words and vibes," said Adam Chambers, MP for Simcoe North in Ontario, during an interview with the BBC on the eve of Carney's speech on Thursday.

Chambers alluded to the existing Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (Ceta) between the EU and Canada, highlighting that it still awaits ratification by multiple EU nations.

And while deepening ties with Europe would be welcomed by many Canadians, there is still a sense that the country's relationship with the US - however strained - must not crumble.

"I grew up here. I've been here 40 years in Canada, in Ontario, and America's always been the neighbour," says Ahmed Khalil.

Building bridges with Europe makes sense, he said: "I think it brings in more money for Canada and more culture, brings Europeans over, probably solves a lot of problems."

But Canada shouldn't forget its southern neighbour, added Khalil.

"I think both are equally valuable to us," he said. "Both are equally valid."

With additional reporting by Madeline Halpert and James Fitzgerald

articles.title: Celebrity Traitors winner Alan Carr's plans to turn £3.25 million Scottish castle buildings into community cafe and estate shop face bat hurdle; council warns historic potting shed could host roosting bats
articles.summary: UK News: Comedian Alan Carr's plans to transform part of his new Scottish castle into a community cafe and estate shop could face an unexpected hurdle - bats.T.
articles.body: Comedian Alan Carr's plans to transform part of his new Scottish castle into a community cafe and estate shop could face an unexpected hurdle - bats.The Celebrity Traitors winner has been renovating Ayton Castle after purchasing the sprawling property for £3.25 million earlier this year. However, his plans to convert a former potting shed and other ancillary buildings at the historic estate have been delayed amid concerns over the potential presence of roosting bats.A full ecological assessment has been requested by council officers before the planning application can proceed.Council orders bat assessment before plans can move forwardAccording to a report by the Daily Mail, Malcolm Ginns, an ecology officer at Scottish Borders Council, said there was potential for the potting shed to provide a roosting site for bats and called for a daytime assessment."There is potential for the potting shed to host roosting bats and a daytime bat assessment should be undertaken," he said.Ginns added that the assessment could require follow-up bat activity surveys, which would need to be carried out between May and September and could not start later than August.Carr's representatives said a full ecological survey was already under way and that a report would be submitted once the work was complete.Alan Carr's plans for Ayton CastleCarr's proposal would see a collection of derelict traditional buildings converted into a community café and estate shop. The plans also include repair and conservation work aimed at preserving the historic fabric of the buildings.The potting sheds consist of four separate single-storey structures, each around 4m wide and 40m long, running along the northern edge of a former walled garden. The buildings are B-listed and are currently described as being in a partially derelict and dilapidated condition.According to the design and access statement prepared by Lorn Macneal Architects Ltd, the café would occupy the eastern end of the buildings, with the estate shop located next to it.The architects said the café could serve dog walkers and people exploring the estate, while also potentially attracting local residents because there are no similar facilities in the village of Ayton. The café and shop could also become an attraction for narrow-gauge railway enthusiasts once the railway becomes operational.Representatives address ecological and conservation concernsCarr's representatives said the proposed adaptive reuse would take the historical significance of the buildings into account and was intended to prevent further deterioration."Full awareness of the existing building's historical significance is addressed and maintained and the adaptive use proposal sits well within the guidance issued by HES, allowing a long-term sustainable purpose for these estate buildings," they said.They added that the proposal would halt further decay and give the buildings a suitable new use.Addressing the possibility of wildlife inhabiting the structures, Carr's representatives said an ecological study had been commissioned."It is recognised that the building location presents potential for habitation by a potential variety of species," they said."Tweed Ecology are currently undertaking a three-stage survey and their full report will be submitted shortly after the last stage survey has been concluded."No public comments had been submitted as part of the application at the time of the report.Previous work at the castle also under scrutinyCarr's representatives have also acknowledged that some work was carried out by the castle's previous owners without the necessary consent, potentially requiring retrospective applications.They said no recent applications had been submitted for work to the main castle, although some earlier repair work had not been completed or reinstated appropriately.The representatives said Carr was aware of the issues and wanted to work with Scottish Borders Council to ensure the necessary permissions were retrospectively obtained and significant features were properly reinstated.Ayton Castle's grand historyAyton Castle, located close to the English-Scottish border, has a long and turbulent history. The site was originally associated with a medieval fortified tower, or peel, linked to the powerful Home family.Its strategic location made it an important stronghold, and by the late 15th century it was considered one of the strongest places between Berwick and Edinburgh. The castle was captured by the English in 1497, while the nearby village of Ayton gave its name to the Treaty of Ayton, signed that year.The medieval stronghold was eventually replaced by a country house, which was destroyed by fire in 1834. The estate was later purchased by banker William Mitchell-Innes, who commissioned the present castle.The existing building was constructed between 1845 and 1851 by architect James Gillespie Graham, with later additions by David Bryce and James Maitland Wardrop.The castle now boasts 17 bedrooms, nine bathrooms, a five-storey Great Tower, turrets, a private chapel and 106 acres of listed gardens.Carr plans to make Ayton his permanent homeCarr has previously revealed that he plans to relocate permanently to Ayton Castle, with the renovation being documented for a Disney+ series.As part of his efforts to regenerate the estate, he recently held an auction featuring around 400 unwanted items from the property, giving buyers the opportunity to purchase pieces from the historic country house.His purchase of Ayton Castle also generated controversy after he initially spoke about becoming a baron and having his own tartan. His remarks on a podcast drew criticism from some locals, who accused him of cultural appropriation and called him an "invader".Carr later clarified that he had turned down the opportunity to purchase the title.A Disney+ spokesperson confirmed that the option to purchase the Baron title came with the castle, but said Carr had chosen not to take it. The spokesperson also said the estate's gates would remain open to dog walkers and ramblers."Alan Carr is very much looking forward to making Ayton his home and getting to know the local community," the spokesperson said."The gates will remain open for the dog walkers and ramblers to continue enjoying the estate grounds."The spokesperson added that Carr hoped to host events at the castle to help cover its running costs while showcasing the estate and surrounding area with minimal disruption.Carr had previously spoken about his plans for his new home on a podcast, saying he wanted a change after turning 50 and describing the local community as "lovely" and "really small".Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Flowers at 10,600ft: World’s highest twin fields unveiled in Leh
articles.summary: India News: JAMMU/SRINAGAR: On Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s 76th birthday, Ladakh Lieutenant Governor Vinai Kumar Saxena inaugurated the world’s highest and Ind.
articles.body: JAMMU/SRINAGAR: On Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s 76th birthday, Ladakh Lieutenant Governor Vinai Kumar Saxena inaugurated the world’s highest and India’s largest twin flower fields in Leh, at an altitude of 10,600ft, on Thursday as part of the administration’s efforts to diversify agriculture, build skills and create new livelihood opportunities in the Union Territory.Spread across 40 acres at Choglamsar and Stakna, the gardens house more than 25 lakh high-value flowers, including 24 lakh Lilium and 1 lakh Gladiolus. The Choglamsar field was developed in just two months, with plantation beginning on July 16 and the first blooms appearing in the first week of Sept. At Stakna, nearly 1.4 lakh lilies were planted in Aug, with the first blooms expected by Oct-end.Saxena said the initiative was the first experiment of its size and nature at such a high altitude in Leh, adding that its successful execution could pave the way for replication elsewhere in Ladakh. The gardens will open to the public on Sept 18, with an entry fee of Rs 25 for adults and Rs 10 for children, officials said.Floriculture, as a high-value agricultural activity, can complement traditional farming, increase cultivators’ incomes and create opportunities for employment and entrepreneurship, the LG said. The Choglamsar flower park will serve as a training, demonstration and model floriculture centre for farmers and youth, where Lilium, Gladiolus, Tulips and other ornamental flowers will be cultivated for national and international markets.“The facility will provide exposure to modern cultivation techniques, scientific farming practices and improved post-harvest management, enabling farmers to acquire the knowledge and skills required to take up floriculture at farm and village levels,” Saxena said. “Besides functioning as a recreational and educational space for residents and tourists, it will create an ecosystem where not only flowers, but also knowledge, skills and enterprises can grow,” he added.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Kashmir cracks walnut success code, turns to medium-sized, grafted trees
articles.summary: India News: KOKERNAG: In Gohan village, around 100km south of Srinagar, Shabir Ahmad was among many harvesting walnuts from a towering tree. The work has become i.
articles.body: KOKERNAG: In Gohan village, around 100km south of Srinagar, Shabir Ahmad was among many harvesting walnuts from a towering tree. The work has become increasingly difficult. “My back aches now,” Ahmad said. J&K produces 3.5 lakh tonnes of walnuts annually, around 90% of the country’s total output.Like other villagers, Ahmad had no safety gear and he was proud of it. “We have been doing it for centuries,” said Ahmad, also a clerk at a local court. However, the bravado doesn’t help in harvesting seasons. Dr. Mohd Yaqoob Bhat, a surgeon at Paras Hospital in Srinagar, said Valley healthcare units treat dozens of patients each year after falls from walnut trees, some with serious spinal injuries. “There is no mechanism to address the issue,” Bhat said.Ahmad’s younger brother sold one walnut for one rupee and no two fruits are similar. For generations, Kashmir’s walnut trees have been grown from seeds. J&K and Sher-e-Kashmir University of Agricultural Sciences and Technology (SKUAST) are now promoting medium-sized, grafted walnut trees to bring greater uniformity and help the produce compete globally amid competition from soft-shelled varieties grown in California and Chile.The initiative aims to replace scattered plantations with organised orchards of known varieties, allowing farmers to grow more trees in the same area and produce walnuts more consistent in size and color.J&K has about 80,000 hectares under walnut cultivation, most of it made up of seedling-origin trees. “When someone plants a walnut seed in the ground, whatever grows becomes a tree. Every tree is a variety of its own,” Ashfaq A. Pandit, professor and head of fruit science at SKUAST, said. This natural variation, once considered an advantage, has become a challenge in the modern market where buyers seek consistent produce.Traditional walnut trees can take about 15 years to bear fruit without using pesticides. Unlike traditional seedling-origin trees, grafted walnuts belong to known varieties.Imtiyaz Ahmad Lone, professor and head of SKUAST’s Walnut Research Centre, said the university released new walnut cultivars and grafting-based cultivation had spread over nearly 90,000 hectares despite lack of subsidies.Farmers argued, however, that the grafted varieties are no match for the traditional Kashmiri walnut. “It is no match in taste. The new varieties are brittle, tasteless. They are a no-show,” Mohammad Sultan, a Pulwama farmer in the business for 50 years, said.Researchers differed. Lone pointed out that grafted trees have early bearing, give faster returns as orchards and nut quality are uniform. “They have higher productivity and better export potential. There is a gradual opportunity to replace unproductive seedling trees,” he said.The transition has impacted walnut woodcraft industries. Walnut trees cannot be cut in J&K without govt permission. The matter was debated in the assembly in March when CM Omar Abdullah opposed a bill allowing landowners to cut walnut trees on private property. Omar defended the restrictions, saying the law served a broader purpose of conserving walnut and chinar trees.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: In 2005, Derek Jeter assembled three Tampa waterfront lots for $7.7 million and built a 22,000-sq-ft mansion; after selling it for $22.5 million in 2021, the home was marked for demolition
articles.summary: News News: One of the Tampa Bay area's most expensive homes, once owned by former baseball star Derek Jeter, has become a puzzle. Derek Jeter's estate at 58 Baha.
articles.body: One of the Tampa Bay area's most expensive homes, once owned by former baseball star Derek Jeter, has become a puzzle. Derek Jeter's estate at 58 Bahama Circle stands exactly as it did when Tom Brady and Gisele Bündchen vacated it five years ago, except now it is owned by a cryptocurrency trust and no one is living there. In 2022, construction crews were meant to tear down the mansion and build something bigger in its place. The home is still standing untouched, and its future is as unclear as its ownership.The waterfront mansion had many ownersLong before it became one of Tampa's most exclusive celebrity homes, 58 Bahama Circle consisted of independent waterfront lots on Davis Island. Derek Jeter’s company acquired three adjoining lots in 2005 and 2006 for about $7.7 million, according to a report by Mansion Global. The asking price seemed steep for vacant land, but this was prime real estate: 345 feet of bay frontage on a man-made island minutes from downtown. The former New York Yankees captain decided to build a custom mansion on the waterfront parcel. Construction took four years. By 2012, the 22,000-square-foot mansion stood alone as Davis Islands' largest property. The compound included seven bedrooms, a wine cellar, a movie theatre, six-car garage, gym, dock with boat lifts, and an 80-foot pool. A six-foot brick wall surrounded the mega-mansion, with frustrated neighbours nicknaming it the Great Wall of Jeter. For nearly a decade, the mansion sat there. In 2017, Jeter moved to Miami, leaving the half-occupied home. At the same time, Tom Brady needed a place to live.In April 2020, Brady signed with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and needed immediate housing. He called Jeter, and they negotiated a rental arrangement that let Jeter list the place for sale while Brady lived there with his supermodel wife, Gisele Bündchen, and family. The quarterback even joked about it once, calling Jeter his landlord. Soon, Brady won a Super Bowl, and the mansion became the talk of the town.Record-breaking sale and demolition plansBy the end of 2020, Jeter listed the property for $29 million. There were potential buyers, but many thought the price point was high. The mansion stayed on the market through 2021 until finally, in May, an offer came. The final price: $22.5 million. It was the highest price ever paid for a residential property in Tampa. But nobody knew the buyer's name. It never appeared in public records. Instead, a trust called 'Zebb.com Trust' took the title.The mysterious new owner, whoever they were, had grand plans. According to a report by the Tampa Bay Times, a demolition permit was filed by a construction firm. The plan was to tear down Jeter's mansion and build something even larger: a 30,000-square-foot residence designed for a local family. The proposed house was designed to have six bedrooms, nine full bathrooms and 11 half-bathrooms, along with a gym, swimming pool and substantial green space. Construction was expected to take several years. It was supposed to start in 2024. The demolition permit expired in 2023. No new permits followed. The mansion remains standing, as though frozen mid-transition.What happened here remains a mystery. Ellison Construction hasn't filed renewed permits in the three years since the first one lapsed. According to the outlet, public records from Hillsborough County list no activity on the property beyond routine tax matters. In 2023, local entrepreneur Sidd Pagidipati and his wife registered the address as their primary residence, which entitled the trust to a homestead tax exemption. But they haven’t spoken about what happens to the mansion. The future of one of Florida's most expensive homes remains uncertain. Perhaps the most stunning residence in Tampa may be the one nobody wants to either keep or demolish.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? Build Your Legacy with TOI Homes.

articles.title: How to find a cat litter your pet (and you) genuinely love, according to veterinarians
articles.summary: Finding a litter your cat loves establishes good bathroom habits and helps you monitor their health. Here’s what vets recommend looking for, like clumping and tracking.
articles.body: Picking out the best litter for your cat may seem simple at first — as long as they like it enough to use it, anything works… right? But once you start weighing different options, the factors you have to consider pile up: material, particle size, scent, clumping level, dust level and tracking are just a few, in addition to how many cats you have and the type of litter box they use. Not to make the process sound even more challenging, but cats are picky — if they don’t like their litter, they may reject it, which, unfortunately, means going to the bathroom places they shouldn’t. Below, I talked to veterinarians about how to find a litter your cat loves, and I shared tried-and-true recommendations from pet parents like myself. Vets also explain how often to scoop, how to transition to something new, and how to distinguish between cats hating a litter and having a serious health issue. Want more from NBC Selected? Sign up for our newsletter, The Selection, and shop smarter. The best cat litters of 2026 I curated this list of the best cat litters based on my personal experience as a pet parent, recommendations from NBC Selected staff members and veterinarians’ guidance. I included information about how I chose my picks and how to shop for cat litter below. Best litter overall This litter came recommended to me by one of my cats’ fosters — she takes care of at least three kittens at a time year-round, so she’s well-versed in what works for multi-cat homes. I first bought it in 2023 and haven’t looked back — in fact, Amazon says I’ve ordered the largest box 28 times, and I constantly get it at Petco, too. Beyond forming solid clumps that stay together when I scoop, this litter masks odors phenomenally well thanks to neutralizers like baking soda in its formula. There’s two litter boxes in my one-bedroom apartment, but guests always say they’d never know because there’s no scent whatsoever. Also, as its name implies, the litter slides right out of the box without leaving residue behind when I pour it into a trash bag. I never notice dust coming from the litter, and despite it being scented, my cats, both of whom have allergies, haven’t experienced irritation. The only downside is that it tracks, but that’s par for the course with clay litter. Best clay litter Best crystal litter Best plant-based litter Tuft & Paw’s Really Great Cat Litter, which is also a NBC Selected Pet Award Winner, is made from tofu, a.k.a. soybeans. It’s infused with charcoal, which helps neutralize odors, and it comes in larger, log-shaped pellets. I was skeptical about this litter at first because it’s unlike the clay formulas I’m used to, but it quickly impressed me. It truly clumps, making cleaning easier than I expected, but the best part of all is how low-tracking it is. The larger pieces don’t stick to my cats’ paws much, if at all, so it barely escapes the litter box, and I found myself vacuuming much less than usual. The brand says this litter is safe to flush down toilets, but experts recommend against doing so (see more about disposing of cat litter in the FAQ section below). Best paper litter I used this paper litter after my cats were spayed as kittens. Its soft, 100-percent recycled paper pellets look very similar to Tuft & Paw’s tofu ones, and they’re just as low-tracking. They’re also odor-neutralizing since they’re made with baking soda. The litter is absorbent, but it doesn’t clump, so cleaning can be difficult. As the paper absorbs urine, it gets heavy, so I found it easier to dump everything out and start with a fresh batch every few days. Best wood litter Before I tried Ôkocat’s wood litter, I used an option that came as chips and shavings, which didn’t clump and made clean-up difficult. My cats and I prefer this medium-sized granular texture — it clumps, is absorbent and is softer on my cats’ paws when they dig. The litter has a natural woody scent that masks odors, but that may deter some felines, according to the experts I talked to, so pay extra attention to your pet’s bathroom habits if you try this one. Ökocat also makes an unscented version of their wood litter, but it may not get rid of odors as well. Best budget litter Chewy’s Clumping Clay Cat Litter is one of the most cost-effective options Brown has found. She says that there isn’t anything particularly notable about it, but since it works well, has a generally low price point and comes in a big bag that lasts her a while, she continues buying it. The litter clumps and is made with deodorizing ingredients that mask odors. How I picked the best cat litters To pick the best cat litters, I evaluated each option based on the following factors, per veterinarians’ guidance. Material: Cat litter is commonly made from clay, silica crystal, paper, wood or plant-based ingredients like tofu. Material influences everything about a litter, like its texture, absorbency level, weight, clumping ability, scent, dust level and tracking level, plus whether it’s suitable for multi-cat homes and standard v.s. automatic litter boxes. There’s no one “best overall” material because cats (and their owners) have different preferences. I included litters made from various materials on my list to give you a comprehensive overview of what’s on the market.Clumping: Clumping litter is easier to thoroughly clean, which reduces how often you need to replace everything inside the box. I prioritized recommending clumping litters because of this, but some materials inherently don’t clump — I note which ones.Scent: Aim to buy unscented litter, says Dr. Enio Sanmarti, the medical director of VEG ER for Pets in Fort Lauderdale. Cats have a very sensitive sense of smell, and artificial fragrances can deter them from entering their box. Most litters I recommend are unscented, but there are a few exceptions — I explain why I still recommend them.Dust level: Low-dust litter is best for cats and their owners, says Sanmarti. The less fine powder a litter puts into the air, the less it dirties the area around the box, and the less likely it is to irritate your and your cat’s respiratory systems. Some materials are naturally low-dust, like silica crystal, paper and wood, and brands can also formulate litters to be low-dust, which they usually call out on their packaging. I only recommended naturally low-dust litters or litters that specifically say they’re low-dust.Tracking: Tracking happens when pieces of litter stick to your cat’s paws or fur, get carried out of the box and get onto your floors. Speaking from experience, it’s the bane of any cat owner’s existence and calls for constant vacuuming. Tracking is unavoidable to some degree, but litters that have larger, heavier particles track less than those with small, sand-like particles, although cats prefer the latter. I included information about tracking for each of the litters on my list. How to shop for cat litter While shopping for cat litter, experts recommend paying the most attention to the following factors. What are the different types of cat litter? No one type of cat litter is considered the “best overall.” Ultimately, it depends on your cat’s preferences, says Dr. Courtnee Morton, a veterinarian at Chewy. (Editor’s note: The inclusion of products sold by Chewy in this article was made independently of Morton.) Some felines will only use certain types, while others don’t discriminate. In addition to the material itself, particle size, meaning how big or small each individual piece of litter is, matters. Some materials come in different forms, like larger pellets and tiny granules, while others are only available in one. Cats typically like small particles and a fine, sand-like texture, says Vega, but again, every pet is different. Here’s what to know about some of the most popular types of cat litter. Clay litter is the most common type, and often, it’s the lowest-priced. It has a small particle size, and you can buy highly absorbent options that form clumps, making scooping easier and offering superior odor control, says Vega. The downsides are that clay litter is heavy, usually tracks outside the box and can be dusty. Silica crystal litter is more lightweight and less dusty than clay, says Morton, adding that it’s an ideal alternative for cats who are sensitive to dust. It’s highly absorbent, too — Morton says silica crystal can hold liquid up to 40 times its weight, so it keeps the litter box dry and successfully controls odors. The main cons are that it doesn’t clump, can track and the texture isn’t always appealing to cats, even though it has a small particle size, says Vega. Many cats gravitate more toward the softer, sand-like feel of clay.Paper-based litter is soft, lightweight, low-dust and low-tracking, plus you can buy it in various forms. That said, it typically comes as larger particles, which some cats don’t like, says Vega. Odor- and moisture-control, as well as clumping ability, is hit or miss.Wood-based litter is absorbant, low-dust and relatively low-tracking, and it comes in various forms. But the particle size is typically larger, and clumping ability and odor-control are iffy. Wood-based litter also feels and smells very different from other types of litter, which can be hard for cats to get used to, says Vega. Plant-based litter can be made from biodegradable materials of small to large particle sizes, like nutshells, tofu (soybeans), corn and wheat. They have natural odor-neutralizing properties, says Morton, and they’re absorbent and lightweight, but their ability to form clumps, control dust and prevent tracking varies. If your cat has food allergies or intolerances, be careful when using a plant-based litter and check its ingredients beforehand. What is clumping cat litter? Clumping cat litter absorbs urine and forms a tight, solid mass that’s easy to scoop out of the box once a day, reducing how often you need to replace everything inside. Since you’re constantly removing what’s dirty, clumping litter reduces odors, too. Non-clumping cat litter, on the other hand, absorbs liquid without forming scoopable clumps, making it challenging to separate urine-soaked litter from clean litter. That means you’ll have to replace everything inside the box more often, especially since it doesn’t trap odors well, says Morton. Overall, clumping litter is more convenient for cat owners in terms of upkeep, which is crucial — cats will avoid a litter box they deem dirty, so the cleaner it is, the more it encourages consistent use. Clumping litter also helps you monitor your cat’s bathroom habits since urine and feces are easier to see, letting you catch irregularities quickly, says Vega. That said, if your cat doesn’t like clumping litter, you’ll have to use a non-clumping option and completely replace what’s inside the box more often. Is it better to use scented or unscented cat litter? Generally, it’s better to use unscented cat litter, says Vega. Scented options have added fragrances that help mask odors so people aren’t bothered by them. But cats have a more sensitive sense of smell than people, so what we find pleasant or subtle might be repulsive to them, says Vega. And if cats don’t like the smell of their litter box, or experience irritation from synthetic fragrances, they may not use it. To reduce odors as much as possible, some litters are made with neutralizing ingredients like activated charcoal and baking soda — prioritize that over added fragrances, vets told me. Cleaning the litter box at least once a day, replacing everything that’s inside as needed and making sure there’s enough litter in the box (at least 2 to 3 inches) is also key to odor-control. Morton added that humidity can reduce a litter’s absorbency and ability to effectively control odors, so if your litter box is exposed to high humidity, you may have to clean the litter more often and use a dehumidifier in that specific room. What is low-dust cat litter? A cat litter’s dust level refers to how much fine powder goes into the air when you pour and scoop it, and when your cat digs around in it, says Morton. Brands label their litter “low-dust” when they formulate it to release as little powder as possible, but it’s all relative — what “low-dust” means is different to each brand, so you’ll have to use a litter to tell how “dusty” it really is. That said, looking for a low-dust litter is important. It keeps the area around the box cleaner and reduces irritation for cats and people who have respiratory sensitivities like asthma or allergies, says Morton. What cat litter is low-tracking? Tracking happens when litter sticks to your cat’s paws and/or fur, causing them to carry it out of the box and onto your floors. Some litters track less than others, like those that have larger, heavier particles, says Vega. They can’t stick to cats’ paws and/or fur as easily, so there’s less of a chance that they leave the litter box. No litter is completely track-free, but the lowest tracking litters are paper-, wood- and plant-based pellets, says Vega. However, many cats prefer litter with small particles and a fine, sand-like texture, so it’s important to use one that aligns with their preferences, not yours. To reduce tracking, you can mix a litter that has larger, heavier particles with one that has smaller particles if your cat doesn’t mind. What’s the best litter for kittens? The best litter for kittens is typically a non-clumping plant-, wood- or paper-based option. Young cats are more likely to lick particles off their bodies and eat unfamiliar materials, so choosing a “natural” litter can help reduce the risk of digestive issues if they swallow anything, says Morton. What’s the best litter for senior cats? The best litter for senior cats is whatever they’re most comfortable and familiar with, says Vega. Keeping their litter consistent helps you identify sudden changes in bathroom habits, which can be a sign of medical issues. If you change their litter, you might mistake your pet having a health problem for not liking their new litter. Meet our veterinary experts At NBC Selected, we work with experts who have specialized knowledge and authority based on relevant training and/or experience. We also ensure that all expert advice and recommendations are made independently and with no undisclosed financial conflicts of interest. Dr. Tom Vega is the DVM ambassador at Roo, and the founder and chief medical officer of Concierge Companions Vet Med.Dr. Courtnee Morton is a veterinarian at Chewy. (Editor’s note: The inclusion of products sold by Chewy in this article was made independently of Morton.)Dr. Enio Sanmarti is the medical director of VEG ER for Pets in Fort Lauderdale. Why trust NBC Selected? I’m a reporter at NBC Selected who has covered pet products for over six years. I’ve written numerous articles about cats specifically, including those about cat food, cat treats, cat toys and cat travel carriers. To write this article I interviewed three veterinarians about different types of cat litter and what to focus on while shopping, as well as asked them some of the most common cat litter-related questions. I also have two cats myself, and I’ve volunteered with stray cats at local animal shelters for years. articles.title: Indian migrant becomes first person in UK charged with advertising illegal immigration services online
articles.summary: Other News News: LONDON: An Indian migrant has become the first person in the UK to be charged under a new law aimed at tackling illegal immigration.Hem Raj (24), an I.
articles.body: LONDON: An Indian migrant has become the first person in the UK to be charged under a new law aimed at tackling illegal immigration.Hem Raj (24), an Indian national who lives in Smethwick, in the West Midlands, has been charged with creating online material promoting unlawful immigration to Britain, a new offence under Section 17 of the Border Security, Asylum and Immigration Act 2025.Section 17 came into force on Feb 2, 2026, introducing an offence that criminalises the creation or publication of material whose purpose is to promote unlawful immigration services on an internet service. The maximum sentence is five years in prison, a fine, or both.Raj is accused of publishing social media posts offering advice to foreign nationals on fraudulent visa and asylum applications. It is the first time someone has been charged with the new offence as part of a National Crime Agency investigation.He has also been charged with, between Aug 2024 and Feb 2026, illegally providing immigration advice without the required authority or qualifications, in contravention of Sec 84 of the Immigration and Asylum Act, 1999.Officers arrested Raj in Smethwick on Sept 15 and seized mobile phones. He appeared at Wolverhampton magistrates’ court on Sept 16. His case was sent to Wolverhampton crown court for a plea hearing on Oct 14. He was remanded on conditional bail, which requires him to wear a GPS ankle tag, live at his home address and not use any internet-enabled devices.Sec 17 allows for the prosecution of anyone who has created or published material that promotes unlawful immigration services on an internet service, whether their activity took place in the UK or overseas. UK prosecutors may arrest suspects on arrival in the UK or seek extradition for prosecution.

articles.title: A Virginia teen started with a dessert fundraiser 2 years ago; his youth team has now rescued over 300,000 pounds of food and raised nearly $52,000
articles.summary: US News: What started as a simple dessert fundraiser organised by a teenager two years ago has grown into a student-led volunteer project that has rescued more.
articles.body: What started as a simple dessert fundraiser organised by a teenager two years ago has grown into a student-led volunteer project that has rescued more than 300,000 pounds of food for families across Northern Virginia. Dhevesh Mahes started his sweet treats project to raise money for charity, but the effort soon grew after he connected with local community leaders. He saw how much good food was being thrown away while many local families struggled to afford groceries. Mahes then formed the Nourishin Ninjas, a youth team working directly with Anna Sudha Community Kitchens. According to profile information from nonprofit organisation Points of Light, which named Mahes a Daily Point of Light Award honoree, the youth group has kept more than 300,000 pounds of food from ending up in landfills. Instead, the rescued produce, baked goods and prepared meals are given to families across the region who are facing food insecurity.Mobilising youth volunteers and local partnersThe Nourishin Ninjas has grown largely by bringing together student volunteers from schools in the area. Since starting the project, Mahes has recruited and organised more than 150 young people across the region. The volunteers handle tasks such as collecting surplus food, packing food boxes, managing deliveries and helping with weekly distributions. To keep a steady supply of rescued food, Mahes has created partnerships with more than 10 local businesses, grocery stores and community organisations. These partners donate extra food that might otherwise be thrown away because of limited shelf life or excess stock. The team also focuses on making sure families can easily access the food. Many low-income households may have difficulty travelling to food pantries located far from their homes. To help, Mahes worked with family liaisons at local public schools. These school-based staff members help identify families who need support and arrange for groceries and hot meals to be delivered closer to where they live.Raising funds and expanding community leadershipThe youth project has also worked to build a reliable source of funding. Under Mahes's leadership, the Nourishin Ninjas has raised nearly $52,000 through donations and grants. The money helps pay for operating costs, vehicle transport, storage equipment and emergency food purchases for partner distribution networks. Mahes's community work also led to his appointment as a Youth Advisor on the board of directors at Anna Sudha Community Kitchens. In that role, he helps with outreach plans and promotes greater involvement by students in solving community problems. In an interview with Points of Light, Mahes said his motivation comes partly from his family. He described his grandfather as an important influence who showed him the importance of helping others quietly and without expecting anything in return. "My grandfather helped people simply because it was the right thing to do," Mahes said in the Points of Light feature. Mahes said he hopes the group's work shows how much young people can contribute to their communities right now. He believes teenagers should be seen as active members of civic life rather than only as future leaders who have to wait until they are older. With new business partnerships and fundraising efforts underway, the Nourishin Ninjas continues to expand its weekly food distribution across Northern Virginia.Catch the latest World News and Live updates.
